# Review instructions for ShowRunner

## Settled decisions

These were raised by earlier reviews, checked, and decided. They are not findings. Do not repeat one unless the PR
changes the code it describes so that the decision no longer holds; if it does, say what changed.

### AI review workflow (`.github/workflows/pr-review.md` -> `pr-review.lock.yml`)

- **The workflow comes from `notglossy/agentic-workflows`.** `pr-review.md` is installed with `gh aw add` (its
  `source:` field points there) and refreshed with `gh aw update`; `pr-review.lock.yml` is generated by gh-aw and
  marked `linguist-generated`. Review changes to the `.md` frontmatter and prompt, not the lock file line by line,
  and do not ask for hand edits to the lock file. Prompt and config changes belong in the shared repository; this
  file holds ShowRunner's own notes. A PR that changes the `.md` must also recompile the lock file.
- **Inference goes to OpenRouter (BYOK), not Copilot.** `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` is a literal so gh-aw adds
  `openrouter.ai` to the firewall allow-list for both the review and the threat-detection step. No Copilot
  subscription, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` or `copilot-requests` permission is involved; the compiler skips the
  Copilot token in BYOK mode. The model comes from the `AI_MODEL` repository variable, with a default in the `.md`.
- **API key isolation.** `AI_API_KEY` is only ever `COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY` in `engine.env`, which strict mode
  allows. The generated step passes `--exclude-env COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY` to the sandbox, so the key lives in the
  AWF API proxy sidecar and the agent container sees a dummy key. Do not ask for extra masking or key handling.
- **`GITHUB_TOKEN` stays read-only in the agent job.** `permissions` are `contents: read` and `pull-requests: read`.
  Writes happen in gh-aw's separate safe-outputs job, capped at 15 inline comments and one `COMMENT` review
  (`allowed-events: [COMMENT]`; the Actions token cannot approve in any case).
- **Event and fork guard.** The workflow uses `pull_request`, not `pull_request_target`. The compiled guard rejects
  PRs whose head repository id differs from the base repository, and the `if:` skips drafts. Fork PRs never run.
- **GitHub-hosted runners.** Every job runs on `ubuntu-latest` or gh-aw's `ubuntu-slim` helper runners. There is no
  self-hosted runner in this workflow, so runner-hardening findings do not apply.
- **Review history.** The prompt tells the agent to read the PR's existing review comments and not re-raise
  answered findings. There is no separate digest step to harden.
- **Instructions file read from the PR head, base version wins when it changes.** This file is pulled in with
  `{{#runtime-import? ...}}` from the checked-out PR at run time, and a missing file is skipped rather than failing
  the run. When a PR edits this file, the shared prompt's "Repository instructions" section tells the agent to
  follow the base version instead and review the edit as a change. That guards against a PR rewriting its own
  review rules by accident or through injected text; it is not a security boundary, since same-repo authors can
  also edit `pr-review.md`, whose prompt body is read from the PR at run time too.

### Android shell (`apps/android`)

- **Device token auth.** `ServerClient` sets the `Authorization` header to the word `Bearer`, a space and the
  device token, on registration (when a token is stored) and on every heartbeat, matching the server's
  `bearerToken()` regex. The persisted token is what lets a claimed display re-register after a reboot on a
  server without `DEVICE_SHARED_SECRET`. The sandbox masks that header as `******` (see "Masked tool output" in
  the review prompt); it is not a literal or a broken header.
